name: ukrainian-interface-restates-the-shell
description: A run declared in Ukrainian builds its shell in Ukrainian: the captions inside the quality-and-speed popover are not the English ones. This asserts that the LANGUAGE reached the widget, not any particular Ukrainian spelling - a catalog that translated the strings differently would still pass, and only a run that installed no catalog (leaving the English sources in place) fails here.

steps.note: The gear, so the popover carrying the captions is on screen. PlayerShell.cpp:349-352 builds it from tr("Quality and speed") and wires the click to openSettings().

assertions.note: The popover itself is hidden at construction (ShellWidgets.cpp:146) and popupNear() shows it (ShellWidgets.cpp:307), so visibility - not existence - says the click landed. Without it the caption below could be read off a widget that was never on screen.

The QUALITY caption is built inside qualitySection_, which starts hidden (ShellWidgets.cpp:224) and is only shown by setQualityOptions() when the option list is non-empty (ShellWidgets.cpp:284). The runner hands the dialog one quality entry at the manifest height (ProbeRunner.cpp:591), so this is visible only when the popover really is the one on screen.

The language reached the widget. qualityCaption_ is built from tr("QUALITY") (ShellWidgets.cpp:205) and ShellWidgets.cpp:290-292 re-reads it on LanguageChange, so a run whose catalog failed to install leaves exactly this English source string here and fails. Deliberately not_equals rather than equals: the point is that the catalog was consulted, not that this run guessed the right Ukrainian word.

A second, independent surface of the same fact: the gear's own tooltip is tr("Quality and speed") (PlayerShell.cpp:349, carried into the button by IconButton's ctor at ShellWidgets.cpp:92). It is built and translated independently of the flyout's captions, so a run that translated the popover but not the dock - or that read the caption off a stale string - fails one of the two.
